# Final follow-up review of expression semantics

Review only committed range `ece0c43eeaa80b9d385176f151ff52354ba3e8e8..47f6d18f719a6b5ec20774a82bc0d0e3bf338fad` read-only. Earlier findings are settled: plain/tagged templates, whole-literal identity, trailing commas, combined wildcards, and mechanical renames.

The new commits address six independently reproduced findings: Java class literals, mixed-quote strings, effectful template substitutions, generic calls, function-local alias shadowing, and TypeScript type/non-null suffixes on fresh identities. A final regression also proves function-local pytest imports remain V3 while non-pytest local bindings shadow aliases. Every regression failed before its fix and passes after; targeted tests now total 58.

Check the fixes and look for concrete introduced defects, especially literal-content preservation, template substitution scanning, generic-call false positives, function-scope binding rules, identity suffixes, and unchanged unittest skipTest behavior. Do not re-report the tracked ledger correction, GitHub enforcement, or settled structural suggestions. Return at most three findings, or an empty findings list promptly.

summary: The follow-up fixes correctly handle the six reproduced cases, but three new edge-case defects remain in the new logic: template substitution scanning truncates at the first `}` inside a substitution (missing side-effecting calls), Python comprehension loop variables are wrongly collected as function-local bindings (masking pytest skip calls), and the TypeScript identity-suffix regex over-matches boolean operators as type suffixes.

findings.title: Template substitution scanning truncates at a `}` inside a string or nested literal, missing side-effecting calls
findings.trigger: A JavaScript/TypeScript template literal whose `${...}` substitution contains a `}` before the first side-effecting call, e.g. `expect(`${"}" + foo()}`).toBe(`${"}" + foo()}`)`. The non-greedy `TEMPLATE_SUBSTITUTION = re.compile(r"\$\{(.*?)\}", re.DOTALL)` stops at the `}` inside the string, yielding the substitution `"` instead of `"}" + foo()`.
findings.consequence: The `foo()` call inside the substitution is never scanned, so `template_side_effect` returns False and the assertion is incorrectly flagged as a V5 "new constant or self-comparing assertion". This is a false positive that rejects a legitimate test (the two operands each re-execute a side-effecting call, matching the gate's own "non-pure equality calls pass" contract).
findings.evidence: scripts/check-verification-integrity.py:280 defines the non-greedy substitution regex; scripts/check-verification-integrity.py:293-300 iterates `finditer` matches and calls `c_like_side_effect(mask_c_like(match[1], javascript=True).code)` on the truncated match[1]. Reproduced: `scan_typescript` returns a V5 marker for `expect(`${"}" + foo()}`).toBe(`${"}" + foo()}`)` while `expect(`${Math.random()}`).toBe(`${Math.random()}`)` correctly returns no marker.

findings.title: Python comprehension loop variables are collected as function-local bindings, hiding pytest skip calls
findings.trigger: A test method that contains a comprehension whose target variable shares the name of an imported pytest skip alias, followed by a call to that alias. Example: `from pytest import skip` then, inside `test_works`, `names = [skip for skip in ['a', 'b']]` followed by `skip('not implemented')`.
findings.consequence: In Python 3 comprehension variables are scoped to the comprehension and do not leak into the enclosing function, so the later `skip('not implemented')` resolves to the module-level `pytest.skip` and actually disables the test. `python_function_bindings` records the comprehension target (`ast.Name` with `Store` ctx) as a function binding, so `python_shadowed_calls` treats the call as shadowed and the gate emits no V3 violation — a false negative that lets a newly disabled test escape verification.
findings.evidence: scripts/check-verification-integrity.py:508-509 adds every `ast.Name` with `Store` ctx, and scripts/check-verification-integrity.py:517 recurses into `ast.iter_child_nodes`, which descends into `ListComp`/`SetComp`/`DictComp`/`GeneratorExp` comprehension targets. Reproduced: `scan_python` returns an empty marker list for the example above, whereas a plain `skip('reason')` is correctly flagged.

findings.title: TypeScript identity-suffix regex treats boolean/bitwise expressions as type suffixes, missing self-comparisons
findings.trigger: An identity assertion whose operand starts with an object/array literal and ends with `satisfies`/`as` followed by a boolean or bitwise expression, e.g. `assert.strictEqual({a: 1} satisfies Foo || x, {a: 1} satisfies Foo || x)` or with `&&`.
findings.consequence: Because `|`, `&`, and `-` are permitted in `TS_IDENTITY_SUFFIX`'s type character class (`[\w$.,<>\[\]\s|&-]+`), the suffix `satisfies Foo || x` fully matches and the operand is treated as a fresh object literal with a type suffix, so `self_comparing` returns False. A genuine self-comparison of a boolean expression is not flagged (V5 false negative).
findings.evidence: scripts/check-verification-integrity.py:281 defines `TS_IDENTITY_SUFFIX` with the permissive character class; scripts/check-verification-integrity.py:325-326 applies `TS_IDENTITY_SUFFIX.fullmatch(suffix)` to the text after the closing bracket. Reproduced: `scan_typescript` returns an empty marker list for `assert.strictEqual({a: 1} satisfies Foo || x, {a: 1} satisfies Foo || x)`, while a plain member self-comparison `assert.strictEqual({a: 1}.a, {a: 1}.a)` is correctly flagged.
